title: Adolf Hitler: What Really Happened to His Body?
question: Why did Stalin lie about Hitler's death?
summary: On 30 April 1945, with Soviet troops less than 500 metres away, Adolf Hitler shot himself in the Führerbunker under the Reich Chancellery in Berlin; Eva Braun, whom he had married the day before, took cyanide. Their bodies were burned with petrol in the Chancellery garden and the remains buried in a bomb crater. Soviet investigators found the dental remains, identified by two of his dentist's staff, but Stalin told the world Hitler had escaped. A West German court declared him dead only in 1956; DNA later showed that the skull kept in Moscow belonged to a woman, while the teeth matched Hitler's X-rays.

sentences: At around half past two on the afternoon of 30 April 1945, Adolf Hitler and Eva Braun walked into his small study, deep under Berlin.
Soviet troops were less than 500 metres away.
Within the hour, both of them were dead.
Their bodies were carried up into the garden, doused with petrol, and set on fire.
And yet, for decades, the world argued about what had really happened to Adolf Hitler.
Stalin even said that he was alive, living in Spain or Argentina.
This is the story of his last ten days, and of the hunt for what was left of him.

chapters.title: The Last Birthday
sentences: On 20 April 1945, Hitler's birthday, Soviet artillery shelled Berlin for the first time.
Four days earlier, Soviet forces had crossed the Oder, and attacked the Seelow Heights, the last major defensive line protecting Berlin on that side.
By 19 April, the Germans were in full retreat from the Seelow Heights, leaving no front line.
Since January, Hitler had been living in the Führerbunker, under the garden of the Reich Chancellery.
A month earlier, the cameras had filmed him in that garden, shaking hands with boys of the Hitler Youth.
It was one of the last times he was filmed.
By the evening of 21 April, Red Army tanks had reached the outskirts of the city.
Berlin's last defenders now included old men of the Volkssturm militia, and boys of the Hitler Youth.
That day, Hitler ordered SS general Felix Steiner to counterattack the Soviets.
The counterattack never came.

chapters.title: The Collapse
sentences: At the next afternoon's situation conference, Hitler was told that his orders had not been obeyed.
He suffered a nervous collapse, and launched into a tirade against his generals, calling them treacherous and incompetent.
Then, for the first time, he declared that the war was lost.
He announced that he would stay in Berlin until the end, and then shoot himself.
Later that day, he asked his SS doctor, Werner Haase, about the most reliable method of suicide.
Haase suggested the pistol-and-poison method: a dose of cyanide, combined with a gunshot to the head.
Hermann Göring learned of Hitler's admission of defeat, and sent him a telegram, asking to take over the leadership of the Reich.
Martin Bormann convinced Hitler that it was an attempt to overthrow him.
Hitler sacked Göring from all his offices, and ordered his arrest.
On 28 April, a BBC report reached the bunker: Heinrich Himmler had offered to surrender to the western Allies.
Hitler flew into a rage, ordered Himmler's arrest, and had Himmler's representative in the bunker, Hermann Fegelein, shot.
By then, the Red Army had reached the Potsdamer Platz, roughly a kilometre away.
Hitler had two days left to live.

chapters.title: The Wedding
sentences: Shortly after midnight on 29 April, Hitler married Eva Braun in a small civil ceremony, in a map room inside the bunker.
Braun had been his companion for years, and had refused to leave him.
After a modest wedding breakfast, Hitler took his secretary Traudl Junge to another room, and dictated his last will and testament.
It named Grand Admiral Karl Dönitz as head of state, and Joseph Goebbels as chancellor.
Hitler signed it at four in the morning, and then went to bed.
That afternoon, he learned that Benito Mussolini had been executed by Italian partisans, and his body strung up in Milan.
Hitler had already recorded in his testament that he would not be made a spectacle of.
He had been given capsules of prussic acid, but after Himmler's betrayal, he began to doubt whether they would work.
He ordered Haase to test one on his dog, Blondi.
The capsule worked: the dog died instantly.

chapters.title: 30 April
sentences: Hitler and Braun lived together as husband and wife in the bunker for less than 40 hours.
By 01:00 on 30 April, Field Marshal Wilhelm Keitel had reported that all the forces Hitler had been depending on to rescue Berlin were encircled, or on the defensive.
At around half past two in the morning, Hitler appeared in a corridor where about twenty people, mostly women, had gathered to say goodbye.
He went down the line, shaking hands with each of them.
Late that morning, General Helmuth Weidling, the commander of the Berlin Defence Area, told him the garrison would likely run out of ammunition that night.
The fighting in Berlin, he said, would come to an end within the next 24 hours.
Later, Hitler gave Weidling permission to attempt a breakout.
After lunch with his two secretaries and his cook, Hitler and Braun said goodbye to Bormann, Goebbels and other members of the bunker staff.
Then the couple went into his study.
Some time later, his valet, Heinz Linge, smelled gunpowder smoke.
Linge and Bormann went in, and found the two of them sitting upright on the sofa.
Eva Braun had died from cyanide poisoning.
According to his adjutant, Otto Günsche, Hitler had shot himself in the right temple with his own pistol.

chapters.title: The Fire
sentences: Following Hitler's own instructions, Linge rolled his body up in a blanket, and the two bodies were carried up through the emergency exit, into the Chancellery garden.
There, as Soviet shells fell around them, they were doused with petrol.
The first attempts to light it failed, so Bormann set a roll of papers on fire, and threw it onto the bodies.
The bunker telephone operator, Rochus Misch, later recalled someone shouting that Hitler's body was being burned.
As they caught fire, Bormann, Günsche, Linge, Goebbels and others raised their arms in salute, inside the bunker doorway.
SS guards brought more cans of petrol, and the fire burned from about four o'clock until half past six.
Witnesses said it left something between charred bones and piles of ashes, which fell apart to the touch.
The remains were covered up in a shallow bomb crater.
On the night of 1 May, German radio announced that Hitler had died a hero, defending the capital of the Reich.
In the early hours of 2 May, the Soviets captured the Reich Chancellery.

chapters.title: The Hunt for the Body
sentences: Just before four in the morning on 1 May, General Hans Krebs met the Soviet general Vasily Chuikov, and gave him the news of Hitler's death.
Krebs was trying to negotiate a ceasefire, and to open peace negotiations.
Joseph Stalin was informed thirteen hours after the event.
He demanded unconditional surrender, and wanted confirmation that Hitler was dead.
He ordered SMERSH, the Red Army's counterespionage unit, to find the corpse.
Inside the bunker, Krebs and General Wilhelm Burgdorf committed suicide.
In early May, Hitler's and Braun's dental remains were extracted from the soil of the garden.
By 11 May, two people who had worked for Hitler's dentist, Käthe Heusermann and Fritz Echtmann, had identified them.
Both would spend years in Soviet prisons.
Those teeth are the only portion of Hitler's body that is known to have been found.

chapters.title: Stalin's Lie
sentences: Stalin restricted the release of information to the public.
On 5 June 1945, the Soviets claimed that Hitler's body had been examined, and that he had died by cyanide poisoning.
Four days later, they said they had not actually identified the body, and that Hitler had likely escaped.
When asked in July how Hitler had died, Stalin said he was living in Spain or Argentina.
For years, the Soviets maintained that Hitler had escaped, sheltered by the western Allies, or in Spain, or in South America.
In November 1945, British counter-intelligence sent Hugh Trevor-Roper to investigate.
His report became the book The Last Days of Hitler.
Until the mid-1950s, the FBI and the CIA investigated many claims that Hitler might still be alive, and lent none of them credence.
The secrecy in which those investigations were shrouded helped fuel theories that he had survived.
Finally, a West German court interviewed 42 witnesses, behind closed doors.
In 1956, it issued a death certificate: there could no longer be the slightest doubt that Hitler had ended his life by his own hand.

chapters.title: The Skull
sentences: In 1946, Soviet agents found part of a skull in the crater where Hitler's remains had been buried.
Its left parietal bone had a bullet hole, and Soviet officials believed it was Hitler's.
In 2009, an American archaeologist, Nick Bellantoni, examined it.
The bone seemed very thin for a male, he said, and the sutures seemed to correspond to someone under 40.
A DNA test showed that the skull was that of a woman.
Blood from the sofa contained male DNA, and in 2025, it was confirmed to be Hitler's.
In 2017, a French forensic pathologist, Philippe Charlier, found the dental remains in the Soviet archives.
They were in perfect agreement with X-rays taken of Hitler in 1944.
Even the tartar on them contained only plant fibres, a detail consistent with Hitler's vegetarianism.
The other remains the Soviets had buried in secret were exhumed by the KGB in 1970, cremated, and cast into a river.
Shortly after Hitler's death, the future US president John F. Kennedy wrote in his diary that the dictator had a mystery about him that would live and grow after him.
Of the man who had ruled Germany since 1933, only the teeth are known to have been found.
So why do you think Stalin lied about Hitler's death for so long? Tell me what you think in the comments.
